name: Bidar
headline: Festival-linked child marriages and very weak historic SSLC results; NGOs run 'academic ICU' bridge classes.
summary: Bidar sees child marriages cluster around festivals such as Akshaya Tritiya, prompting special task forces. SSLC outcomes have been historically poor, at one point only 27% passed, and Rotary Clubs have set up 'academic ICU' courses to help out-of-school children clear SSLC before they age out at 16. The district's out-of-school tracking figures are contested.

reasons.detail: Child marriages spike around festivals such as Akshaya Tritiya, so officials form special teams to stop parents withdrawing daughters from Class 8-9.
A Hindu report on the district's results recorded only about 27% passing at one point, a pipeline that pushes failing students out.

Bidar ranked 28th of 35 educational districts in the 2026 SSLC results with a 92.17 percent pass rate, below the state figure of 94.1 percent, per a results aggregator. Exam failure is a recognised exit point at Class 10.

reasons.factor: Enrolled children working in scrap shops
reasons.detail: An official said some enrolled Bidar students worked in a nearby scrap shop and had to be rescued.
A statewide police drive in September 2026 recorded 8 child labour rescue cases in Bidar. The report gives no breakdown of work type or whether the children had left school.

Reporting on the 2025 SSLC results cites missing teachers and infrastructure as drivers of poor Kalyana Karnataka performance. Bidar is not named in that article, so this is regional context rather than district evidence.
